title: GRADIEND: Feature Learning within Neural Networks Exemplified through Biases
claim: A gradient-based encoder-decoder compresses model gradients into one scalar feature neuron that can both read out and edit a learned feature.
layout: 2 panels, left-to-right; training with data on top, inference on right
description: Two-part diagram. Panel (a), the training phase, is wide. At the top is the data: a template sentence, a random name substituted in, and a training instance with a [MASK] token. The mask resolves to 'she' (green check) or 'he' (red cross), which give the gradients ∇+Wm and ∇−Wm. Below, columns of blue-shaded circles show the model weights and gradient vectors being subtracted. They feed an encoder that narrows to a single scalar neuron h, then a decoder that expands back, with an MSE target at the right. Panel (b), the inference phase, shows the encoder with a female/neutral/male readout of h. Beneath it, the decoder output is scaled by a learning rate and a feature factor, then added to Wm to give the changed model. Dashed arrows link the data to the network, and shading shows weight values.
caption: GRADIent ENcoder Decoder (GRADIEND) – Targeted learning of a single scalar feature neuron using orthogonal gradient inputs, shown with an example for gender bias.
abstract: AI systems frequently exhibit and amplify social biases, leading to harmful consequences in critical areas. This study introduces a novel encoder-decoder approach that leverages model gradients to learn a feature neuron encoding societal bias information such as gender, race, and religion. We show that our method can not only identify which weights of a model need to be changed to modify a feature, but even demonstrate that this can be used to rewrite models to debias them while maintaining other capabilities. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach across various model architectures and highlight its potential for broader applications.
